mechanism_narrative: Sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks (from -10.0% to -5.9%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend continuation will drive RETAIL_REC further positive over the next four weeks as baseline suppression erodes.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses to decline more than 2 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (39.4% above baseline) reflects sustained essential-goods shopping behavior. This signals consumer confidence and foot traffic patterns that spill over into adjacent retail-and-recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 35% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM sustained at 37-40% across all four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 30% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite sustained GROCERY_PHARM elevation.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -4% (from -7.6% baseline), indicating restrictions on public transport are easing. Improved transit access removes a friction barrier to retail-and-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -7.6% to -4.3% over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines below -5% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite TRANSIT improvement exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains suppressed (-15.7%) while RESIDENTIAL mobility is elevated (5.3%), indicating people remain home-bound. This constraint on outdoor leisure will persist, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks as consumers lack outdoor activity alternatives.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -10% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 4% simultaneously
failure_condition: PARKS mobility improves above -10% or RESIDENTIAL falls below 3%, or RETAIL_REC increases despite both conditions holding.

mechanism_narrative: Weak WORKPLACES mobility (-2.3%) combined with suppressed PARKS (-15.7%) indicates limited commuting and outdoor recreation. This dual suppression constrains retail foot traffic from both work-commute and leisure pathways, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -2% and PARKS below -15% in the same week
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES rises above 0% or PARKS rises above -10%, or RETAIL_REC increases more than 3 percentage points despite both proxies remaining suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July timing in Singapore coincides with school holidays and potential summer leisure demand. GROCERY_PHARM elevation (39.4%) combined with stabilizing TRANSIT (-4.3%) creates conditions for family-oriented retail-and-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC positive over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 38% and TRANSIT above -5% in the same week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 37% or TRANSIT falls below -6% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -13.6% (t-2w) to -2.3% (t-0w), signaling workplace reopening. This workplace recovery will drive commute-time retail visits and weekday foot traffic, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as work-based mobility patterns normalize.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 percentage points from prior week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 11.3 percentage points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines below -5% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite sustained WORKPLACES recovery above -3%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (5.3%) persists despite RETAIL_REC improvement, indicating home-based activity remains the dominant pattern. This persistent residential preference will constrain RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks, capping recovery despite other mobility improvements.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL sustained at 5.3-7.6% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases more than 5 percentage points despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated above 5%.
